task: Implement Cursor IDE OTLP hook forwarding: bypass the shared hook pipeline for cursor-ide via a new AgentHookConfig.otlpIngestion flag, fire-and-forget forward raw hook events to the local proxy daemon over a new /v1/otlp/hook-events route, remove the superseded capture mechanism and dead cursor-ide code, and add a proxy plugin that appends events to ~/.codemie/logs/hook-events.jsonl.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches four distinct components/subsystems: the shared hook CLI pipeline (hook.ts bypass branch plus removal of dead handler cases and the captureEvent read site), the cursor-ide agent plugin (metadata rewrite plus deletion of its hook-transformer/types/event-log modules and a new forwarder module), the proxy connect-orchestrator (daemon-identity union extended, an early-return fast path removed), and the proxy plugin pipeline (a new core ProxyPlugin/ProxyInterceptor). Matches the project calibration anchor profile-provider-decoupling.json (component_scope XL/5 for a comparable 4+ subsystem spread) and the bundled epmcdme-10303 cloud-service example (component_scope XL/5, 'full stack + external service').

No exact precedent for a full hook-pipeline bypass; base risk already elevated by the fire-and-forget forwarder writing to a shared daemon. Bumped +1 per the security-sensitivity auto-bump: the new OtlpIngestPlugin persists the raw Cursor payload verbatim to a global, per-user file (~/.codemie/logs/hook-events.jsonl) with no sanitization applied to this surface, unlike the deleted cursor-ide.event-log.ts mechanism it replaces which did sanitize/truncate before writing — any secret or PII in a tool's stdout/stderr/diff is now durably persisted unsanitized. Bumped a further +1 per the enumerated-edge-case auto-bump: the technical analysis names five new/changed production behaviors (hook bypass branch, forwarder, proxy plugin, daemon-identity branch, dispatch change) with specific enumerated failure modes (401/400/500 on the route, timeout/dead-pid on the forwarder) and zero test coverage for any of them, despite the repo having an established, directly-applicable test pattern (co-located plugin tests, connect-orchestrator's mock-and-assert pattern) for each — and this gap already let a real, shipped regression (the missing runCursorIde dispatch call) through uncaught. This is evidence-based, not speculative, unlike the bundled XL cloud-service example's risk=5 which is mitigation-covered (circuit breaker, credential management).

Roughly 11 files touched: modified (AgentHookConfig types.ts, hook.ts, cursor-ide.plugin.ts, connect-orchestrator.ts, connectors/cursor-ide.ts, proxy plugins/index.ts), new (cursor-ide.otlp-forwarder.ts, otlp-ingest.plugin.ts), deleted (cursor-ide.event-log.ts, cursor-ide.hook-transformer.ts, cursor-ide.types.ts), across six directories (agents/core, agents/plugins/cursor-ide, cli/commands, cli/commands/proxy, cli/commands/proxy/connectors, providers/plugins/sso/proxy/plugins) — matches the 11-15 file / multiple-subsystem XL band. No schema-migration red flag applies here (unlike the profile-provider-decoupling anchor, which bumped this dimension to XXL for a data migration), so it stays at XL rather than bumping further.

Five layers touched in a single commit: the hook CLI layer (bypass branch), the agent plugin layer (declarative metadata + new forwarder), the proxy orchestrator/service layer (daemon-identity derivation, dispatch change), the infrastructure/daemon layer (always-ensure-a-daemon invariant), and a new API route plus persistence sink in the proxy plugin pipeline (/v1/otlp/hook-events -> hook-events.jsonl). Matches the XL criterion 'full stack plus an integration layer, cross-cutting concerns added in several layers.'

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped +1: unsanitized raw hook payload (potential secrets/PII) persisted verbatim to a global per-user file (~/.codemie/logs/hook-events.jsonl) with no sanitization util applied to this new persistence surface, replacing a deleted mechanism that did sanitize.

Technical Risk bumped +1: five new/changed production behaviors ship with zero test coverage despite an established, directly-applicable test pattern for each and despite explicit enumerated failure modes (401/400/500, timeout, dead-pid) in the design — this gap already let a real shipped regression (missing runCursorIde dispatch call, breaking .cursor/hooks.json generation) through uncaught.
